title: Fragmented Ask Threads and Probe Playbook — Sep 2026
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight synthesis of ~30 recent customer threads that do not fit neatly into previous CS buckets. Goal: surface small-LOE probes we can run to validate demand, clarify scope, and inform roadmap tradeoffs for product and infra.

TL;DR:
- Customers keep surfacing three semi-related friction spaces: routing & fallbacks, predictable latency under burst, and observability for per-request economics.
- Most asks are micro-features or configuration knobs, not full product rewrites — good candidates for 2–6 week probes.
- Quick probes: (1) a fallback policy template + docs, (2) per-route recent-percentile latency telemetry, (3) a sample config for conservative batching that preserves 95p latency.

Customer vignettes (anonymized) — representative threads:
1) SaaS analytics startup: sees tail latency spikes during nightly batch jobs; asks for better guidance on batching config and a way to pin requests to dedicated-GPU pool when spike expected.
   - Quote: "We'd accept slightly higher cost if we could guarantee a 200ms 95p during sync windows."
2) Fintech platform: concerned about silent quality regressions after model swaps; wants a 'dry-run' routing that sends a shadow copy to the new variant and surface token-delta and similarity metrics.
   - Current workaround: manual A/B for a small sample set; painful to operationalize.
3) Customer success team reports multiple customers asking for more transparent per-request cost breakdown in console and via API so they can tie LLM spend to product features.

Synthesis: request clusters and suggested probes
A. Routing & failover patterns (high frequency)
   - Asks: more granular policies (by route, by customer tier), templates for canary/auto-fallback, dry-run shadowing.
   - Probe: Build a "fallback policy starter kit" (docs + config examples + 1-click canary toggle) and ship to 5 pilot customers.
   - Success signal: 5 pilot customers adopt, reduction in manual rollback incidents by 40% over 6 weeks.

B. Latency predictability during bursts (moderate frequency but high impact)
   - Asks: deterministic SLO behavior, conservative-batching options, explicit reserve capacity hints.
   - Probe: Create a sample conservative-batching config and a scheduler doc for predictable 95/99p; run with 2 customers during scheduled traffic storms.
   - Engineering risk: scheduler changes could affect throughput; need SRE signoff.

C. Per-request economics and observability (recurring ask)
   - Asks: token-level cost per request, attribution to features/routes, exportable CS-friendly CSVs.
   - Probe: Add a lightweight per-route CSV export prototype (fields: route, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, quant_profile, cost_estimate) and test UX with two customers.
   - Notes: privacy concerns — strip PII; consult security.

D. Quality regression detection (lower volume but impactful)
   - Asks: automated smoke evals on model rollouts + alerting when generation drift exceeds thresholds.
   - Probe: Automate a small eval harness that runs 100 golden prompts on new model variants, compute lexical and semantic drift (embedding cosine), and create a pass/fail gate in rollout.

Low-effort quick wins (<= 2 weeks)
- Ship a one-page fallback policy playbook (markdown doc + examples). Owner: CS; reviewer: Product-hosted-api. Linked Jira: CS-5123.
- Add a console label that surfaces current route's 95p latency from last 24h. Owner: Observability; small UI change.
- Draft sample conservative-batching YAML and share in community Slack for feedback.

Medium-effort probes (2–6 weeks)
- Per-route CSV export prototype + small API endpoint (engineering + CS pilot). JIRA: CS-5139.
- Shadow/dry-run routing prototype that captures token-delta metrics and stores to a private metrics store for analysis.

Risks & constraints
- Cost transparency requires careful wording and possibly legal review for externalizing cost formulas.
- Scheduler/batching changes need load-testing; risk of throughput reduction.
- Shadowing increases metric volume and may require temporary quota increases.

Open questions (need clarifying research)
- What minimal set of fields do customers need to make spend decisions? (Action: CS survey; target 10 responses by 2026-09-29)
- For shadowing/dry-run, are customers comfortable with latency overhead? (Action: pilot with two low-latency-tolerance customers)
- Should conservative-batching be a per-route config or per-deployment template? (Action: product+infra design session)

Suggested next steps and owners
1) Create fallback policy playbook draft — Owner: Priya Nambiar; Due: 2026-09-24; Jira: CS-5123.
2) Prototype per-route CSV export (backend stub + small UI) — Owner: Liam Chen; Due: 2026-10-07; Jira: CS-5139.
3) Run a 2-customer conservative-batching storm test — Owner: Marco Ruiz; Due: 2026-10-14.
4) CS-run survey on cost fields — Owner: Ava Martinez; Due: 2026-09-29.

Notes to self / loose threads:
- Link to prior "Signal Board" doc for context: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/CS/Signal-Orchard-Notes
- Capture pilot customer contacts in CRM before outreach (SalesOp ticket needed).
- Check with Security on permitted export schema for per-request cost CSVs.

Appendix — raw snippets from threads (anonymized)
- "We don't want a black box — show token breakdown by feature so we can bill feature X to customers."
- "Can we run a new model variant in shadow and only route 5% traffic? We need to see drift metrics before promoting."
- "What knobs exist to avoid 99p spikes when we get sudden batch traffic?"
